questions.q: For Group 1 structures (Simplest Utilization, e.g., Hangars), what is the BPF percentage for a project with a Project Construction Cost (PCC) of Php 50M and below?
o: 3% of the PCC
5% of the PCC
10% of the PCC
6% of the PCC
questions.n: Group 1 structures involve simpler spatial requirements and less technical coordination, justifying the 5% base rate.

questions.q: In Group 2 (Moderate Complexity, e.g., Art Galleries, Nursing Homes), what is the BPF percentage for a project with a PCC of Php 50M and below?
o: 6% of the PCC
8% of the PCC
5% of the PCC
7% of the PCC
questions.n: Moderate complexity buildings require a 6% fee to cover the increased coordination and detailing needed.

questions.q: For Group 3 (Exceptional Complexity, e.g., Mental Institutions, Laboratories), what is the BPF percentage for a project with a PCC of Php 50M and below?
o: 6% of the PCC
10% of the PCC
12% of the PCC
7% of the PCC
questions.n: Highly specialized buildings require advanced technical expertise, resulting in a 7% base fee.

questions.q: If a Group 2 project has a PCC of Php 100M, the fee for the first 50M is 6%. What percentage is applied to the excess over 50M?
o: 6% of the excess
4% of the excess
3% of the excess
5% of the excess
questions.n: Under SPP Doc 202, the second tier for Group 2 (over 50M to 100M) drops to 5%.

questions.q: Which building group includes structures specifically classified as 'Public Markets' and 'Freight Depots'?
o: Group 1
Group 2
Group 4
Group 3
questions.n: These are utilitarian structures with simple space utilization and repetitive framing.

questions.q: When providing a 'Statement of Probable Construction Cost,' is the architect allowed to guarantee the final cost to the client?
o: Yes, to build client trust
Yes, if the contingency is at least 20%
Only if the architect is also the contractor
No, they only provide a professional estimate
questions.n: The architect provides 'Probable' costs; only the contractor's bid or a fixed-price contract can define the cost.

questions.q: If a client requests a design that violates the National Building Code, what is the architect's ethical duty?
o: Advise the client against it and refuse to participate in the violation
Follow the client's instructions since they are paying
Find a loophole to bypass the regulation
Proceed but sign a waiver of liability
questions.n: The architect's duty to the law and public safety supersedes the client's desires.

questions.q: Can an architect accept a commission or 'kickback' from a supplier for a material they recommended?
o: No, the architect must only accept compensation from the client
Yes, if they use the money for the project's benefit
Yes, it is a common industry perk
Only if the amount is less than 5% of the material cost
questions.n: This ensures the architect's recommendation is based on the project's needs, not personal profit.

questions.q: What must an architect do if they have a financial interest in a company bidding for the client's project?
o: Keep it secret to avoid bias
Award the bid to their company to ensure quality
Resign from the project immediately
Disclose the conflict of interest to the client immediately
questions.n: Transparency allows the client to make an informed decision about the architect's impartiality.

questions.q: At what point in the relationship must the architect define the scope of work and professional fees?
o: After the Schematic Design is approved
Upon project completion
At the very beginning, through a written Service Agreement
When the Building Permit is issued
questions.n: RA 9266 and the Code of Ethics mandate a clear agreement before services are rendered.

questions.q: When seeking work through advertisements, what is the architect prohibited from using?
o: A list of past projects
Contact information and office address
Self-laudatory, exaggerated, or misleading statements
The title 'Registered and Licensed Architect'
questions.n: Advertising must be factual and dignified, not boastful or deceptive.

questions.q: What is the architect's duty regarding 'Sustainable Development'?
o: To promote and include sustainable design to protect the environment
Only to apply it for LEED-certified projects
To ignore it if it increases the construction cost
It is optional and should only be done if the client asks
questions.n: The architect acts as a steward for the future by minimizing the ecological footprint of buildings.

questions.q: If an architect discovers a structural defect in a building that poses a danger to the public, what is their duty?
o: Wait for the Building Official to find it
Inform the media first
Report the danger to the proper authorities and the owner
Do nothing if they are not the Architect-of-Record
questions.n: The 'Public Welfare' clause requires the architect to prioritize safety above all else.

questions.q: How should an architect participate in civic affairs?
o: By using their influence to get government contracts
By sharing technical knowledge for community improvement
By avoiding all community activities to focus on work
Only by paying their taxes
questions.n: Architects should contribute to better urban planning, housing, and public space in their communities.

questions.q: Can an architect offer their services for 'free' to compete for a public project?
o: Only if the other architects also offer free sketches
Yes, to get exposure for a new firm
No, this is considered unethical 'unfair competition'
Yes, if it is for the government
questions.n: Competing through 'free' services devalues the profession and creates a race to the bottom.

questions.q: When interpreting contract documents, what is the architect's primary duty to the contractor?
o: To provide the contractor with shortcuts to save time
To always side with the owner
To ignore minor errors in construction
To be fair and impartial as a quasi-judicial officer
questions.n: In disputes or interpretations, the architect must judge based on the facts of the documents.

questions.q: What should an architect do if the contractor requests a 'Change Order' for work shown in the original plans?
o: Tell the contractor to skip that part of the work
Ask the owner to pay half of it
Deny it and clearly explain the existing plans
Approve it to keep the contractor happy
questions.n: If the work was already in the scope, it is not a 'change' and should not cost extra.

questions.q: Is it ethical for an architect to deliberately delay the processing of a contractor's 'Certificate of Payment'?
o: No, they must process certifications promptly if work is compliant
Yes, if the contractor was rude to the architect
Yes, to help the owner manage cash flow
Only if the architect is busy with another project
questions.n: Delaying payment for completed, compliant work is an abuse of power and unethical.

questions.q: How should an architect handle a situation where a contractor makes an honest mistake in the construction?
o: Demand the contractor be fired immediately
Cover up the mistake so the owner doesn't see it
Assist in finding a technical solution that is fair to both parties
Charge the contractor a penalty fee for the architect's time
questions.n: Collaboration to maintain project quality while acknowledging human error is the professional approach.

questions.q: What is the architect's duty regarding 'Shop Drawings' submitted by the contractor?
o: To review and approve them with reasonable promptness
To redesign the parts shown in the shop drawings
To charge the contractor an extra fee for each review
They are the contractor's problem and don't need review
questions.n: Prompt review prevents construction delays and ensures materials meet specifications early.

questions.q: What is the architect’s duty regarding the 'Diversified Experience' (Logbook) of their subordinates?
o: To only let the intern do drafting work for two years
To sign it at the end of the year without checking
To provide well-rounded training and accurately certify hours
To charge the intern for the mentorship
questions.n: The mentor ensures the intern gains experience in design, documentation, and site visits.

questions.q: Is it ethical for an architect to underpay their subordinates or use them as 'free labor'?
o: Yes, if the intern needs the experience
No, the architect must provide just and adequate compensation
Yes, but they must provide free lunch
Only for the first six months
questions.n: The Code of Ethics explicitly protects employees from exploitation.

questions.q: What is the architect's duty regarding the 'Professional Credit' of a subordinate who contributed significantly to a design?
o: Acknowledge the contribution and not take sole credit
Credit is only for the people who pay for the project
Wait until the subordinate becomes an RLA to give credit
The principal architect always takes sole credit
questions.n: Ethical architects recognize the collaborative nature of the design process.

questions.q: Can an architect prevent a subordinate from leaving the firm to start their own practice?
o: Yes, if they haven't finished their logbook
No, but the subordinate must not take proprietary files without permission
Only if they signed a 10-year non-compete clause
Yes, by holding their license hostage
questions.n: Freedom of movement is a right, but intellectual property must be respected.

questions.q: What should an architect do to help their subordinates pass the board exam?
o: Give them extra work to test their stamina
Act as a mentor and allow time for study preparation
Tell them to figure it out on their own
Prohibit them from taking the exam to keep them in the firm
questions.n: A good mentor supports the transition of their staff into licensed peers.
